question: Should core Skill Workshop permanently expose the new `review` action and optional `proposal_version` lifecycle contract?
rationale: The patch is technically plausible, but adding model-facing tool and approval API surface is a product and ownership choice that tests cannot authorize.

options.title: Approve the core contract
options.body: Keep the portable preview and version binding after real-flow proof and a current-main refresh.

options.title: Narrow the API
options.body: Preserve exact previewing while reducing or redesigning the public lifecycle parameter surface before merge.

options.title: Decline the feature
options.body: Retain the existing inspect and metadata-only approval workflow and close the linked feature request.

recommendation.title: Approve the core contract
recommendation.body: Keep the portable preview and version binding after real-flow proof and a current-main refresh.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main integration history is the strongest available routing signal for the newly introduced core Skill Workshop surface.
